import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Gromov's theorem on groups of polynomial growth

*Reference:*
 - [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gromov%27s_theorem_on_groups_of_polynomial_growth)
-/

/-
Note: this was obtained in work with Kasia Jankiewicz and Catherine Pfaff, and using
Claude 4.0 Sonnet: https://claude.ai/share/918bb269-bd28-4c09-b84e-cab579c836e8
-/

namespace GromovPolynomialGrowth

open Filter

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- Infinite groups do not satisfy polynomial growth over `ℕ` for any degree `d` because when
`d = 0` this reduces to the unbounded nature of `growthFunction` while `n = 0` works when `d ≠ 0`.
Thus a finitely-generated infinite nilpotent group would be a counter-example to
Gromov's theorem when quantifying over all of `ℕ`, and so `n = 0` should be excluded. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem growthFunction_not_polynomial_of_infinite [Infinite G] {S : Set G} (hS : S.Finite)
    (h : Subgroup.closure S = ⊤) {C : ℝ} (d : ℕ) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ), C * n ^ d < GrowthFunction S n := by
  by_cases hd : d = 0
  · obtain ⟨n, _, hn⟩ := exists_lt_of_tendsto_atTop (tendsto_atTop_growthFunction_of_infinite hS h)
      0 ⌈C⌉₊
    use n
    grw [Nat.le_ceil C]
    simpa [hd] using mod_cast hn
  · exact ⟨0, by simp [hd, growthFunction_zero]⟩

variable (G)

/-- **Gromov's Polynomial Growth Theorem** : A finitely generated group has
    polynomial growth if and only if it is virtually nilpotent. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem GromovPolynomialGrowthTheorem [Group.FG G] :
    HasPolynomialGrowth G ↔ Group.IsVirtuallyNilpotent G := by
  sorry

end GromovPolynomialGrowth

reformulations.difference: Polynomial growth is expressed using a positive monomial bound C*n^d only for n > 0, with inverses allowed implicitly in the generating alphabet. Wikipedia uses a polynomial bound relative to a symmetric generating set. Mathlib also defines nilpotence through the upper central series rather than the lower central series.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Symmetrizing S preserves its generated subgroup and every Cayley ball. A monomial bound for positive radii gives the polynomial bound 1 + C*n^d at every natural radius, since the radius-zero ball has cardinality 1. Conversely, every real polynomial is bounded above by some positive monomial for integral n ≥ 1. Upper-central-series termination is equivalent to lower-central-series termination, and Subgroup.FiniteIndex is equivalent to finiteness of the coset space. The complete equivalence with this source formulation was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using the admitted Gromov theorem.

sources_consulted: Bruce Kleiner, A new proof of Gromov's theorem on groups of polynomial growth, arXiv:0710.4593v4, LaTeX source, especially §1.1: https://arxiv.org/e-print/0710.4593
Checked-out Mathlib sources: GroupTheory/Finiteness.lean, GroupTheory/Nilpotent.lean, GroupTheory/Index.lean, Algebra/Group/Subgroup/Lattice.lean, and Data/Set/Card.lean.
review.notes: Both declarations were checked. The research-solved category agrees with the source. The auxiliary test correctly identifies the failure of an unshifted positive-degree monomial bound at radius zero; its degree-zero case follows from unbounded growth. Lean checks covered empty generating sets, trivial and finite groups, a two-element group, and satisfiable infinite-group hypotheses. Finite generating sets ensure all relevant Cayley balls are finite, so Set.ncard's infinite-set default cannot affect the claim. The final scratch file compiles; the source-equivalence proof and the auxiliary theorem have no sorryAx dependency.
